title: Session-aligned retention with legal-hold and sampled audit traces
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: customers need retention controls that align with interactive sessions (chat/conversation sessions) so that prompts, model responses, request logs, and derived metrics can be retained or expired as a single logical unit. They also need legal-hold overrides and a lightweight sampled audit trail for long-term compliance without incurring full storage costs. Scope: implement session-aligned TTLs, legal-hold flagging and release workflow, and sampled audit export for sessions older than retention window. Out of scope: cross-region rehydration, deep archival tooling (handled by separate archival project). Constraints: must work with Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes; respect per-tenant data residency; integrate with existing evidence export format; not require schema migrations for the primary request store. Acceptance criteria below define success.
acceptance_criteria: Ability to set a session-level TTL that applies to all artifacts generated within the session (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics).
Legal-hold flag can be applied at session or tenant level and prevents deletion until explicit release; hold state is audit-logged and visible in Console.
Sampled audit trail exports sessions using configurable sampling rate and retention for long-term evidence (S3/Blob) with provenance metadata.
Retention enforcement runs within SLA (deletions within 24h of schedule) and exposes per-tenant retention state and backlog in Console.
Retention decisions respect tenant data-residency rules (no cross-region copies during export unless tenant allows).
API endpoints and Console UI for setting session TTLs, placing/removing legal-holds, and configuring sampling are implemented and documented.
engineering_notes: Spike (ENG-22456) showed two viable approaches: tag-based expirations at write time vs explicit session tombstone records. Tombstone approach preferred to avoid changing request store compaction logic.

Will add session_id field (existing sessions table) to retention index; retention service polls tombstones and enqueues deletes to backfill job. No primary table schema change required for request_logs where session_id already exists.
Sampling engine will reuse existing metrics export pipeline; add provenance headers (session_id, sampling_rate, exporter_checksum).
Legal-hold will be stored in tenant metadata service and mirrored to the retention index; release workflow requires two-step confirmation in Console and an audit PR to security logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): implement tombstone-based enforcement and API; run E2E against staging with synthetic tenants (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (beta): enable opt-in for enterprise tenants with legal-hold needs; collect telemetry and failed deletion rates (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): enable Console controls, sampling UI, and documentation; provide migration playbook for on-prem customers (2 weeks).
